issues.legal_issue: An execution court commits a material irregularity in conducting an auction sale when it fails to judicially consider objections and purchaser-relevant particulars for the sale proclamation.
material_facts: The judgment-debtors gave their own valuations of the two bungalows, objected to selling them together, and sought a commission at their expense to report on matters affecting value.

The execution court rejected the judgment-debtors’ valuations as exaggerated and effectively adopted the decree-holders’ valuations without giving reasonable grounds or adequately considering the objections.
The sale proclamation omitted the area of the compound and the unexpired lease period and rent, and did not specify whether the bungalows would be sold together or separately.
The execution court did not judicially decide whether the bungalows could be sold separately or what particulars should be included in the proclamation.
issues.conclusion: The execution court failed to perform its duty fairly and reasonably, and the sale of the two bungalows involved a material irregularity.
issues.legal_principle: Order 21, Rule 66(2)(e), Civil Procedure Code, requires the court to include essential facts that would assist a purchaser in judging the nature and value of the property. The court should normally state both parties’ valuations when neither appears fantastic, consider relevant objections, and identify other useful material particulars on the facts of the case. It need not state its own valuation or insert a reasoned judicial order in the proclamation, but its order must show that it applied its mind and did not merely accept one side’s assertions. The court reviewed decisions including S. K. Veeraswami Pillai v. Kalvanasundaram Mudaliar, A.M.K.M. Firm v. Baishmaw, Charandas Vasanji v. Dossabhoy Maganlal, and Sitabai Rambhau Marathe. It did not decide whether the decree-holders’ conduct amounted to actual fraud.

rule.if: execution_auction_sale_challenge and competing_property_valuations_present and court_accepted_one_side_without_reason and purchaser_relevant_details_omitted and sale_configuration_objection_unconsidered

predicates.execution_auction_sale_challenge: A party challenged the conduct of an auction sale held to execute a decree.
predicates.competing_property_valuations_present: The parties presented different valuations of the property being sold.
predicates.court_accepted_one_side_without_reason: The court adopted one side’s valuation without giving reasonable grounds for preferring it over the other side’s valuation.
predicates.purchaser_relevant_details_omitted: The sale proclamation omitted facts about the property that could reasonably help a purchaser assess its nature or value.
predicates.sale_configuration_objection_unconsidere: The court did not consider an objection about whether the property should be sold together or in separate lots.

issues.definition: When an execution auction sale is challenged and the parties provide different valuations, the court adopts one without reason, relevant property details are omitted, and an objection about the sale lots is left unconsidered, the sale is materially irregular.

issues.legal_issue: A material irregularity in an execution sale warrants setting it aside when the judgment-debtor proves substantial injury resulting from the sale.
material_facts: The three houses in another sale item were put up separately and realised a total price considerably greater than the value attributed to them when grouped together in the proclamation.
The High Court found that the two bungalows would probably also have fetched a higher price if sold separately.
The judgment-debtors’ assertions about the value and sale of comparable property were not controverted by material from the decree-holders.
The Court found enough evidence of substantial injury from the sale of the two bungalows.
issues.conclusion: Substantial injury was shown as to the sale of the two bungalows; the Court set that sale aside and ordered a fresh sale after judicial consideration of whether the bungalows could be sold separately and what particulars should be included in the proclamation.
issues.legal_principle: In an application under Order 21, Rule 90, Civil Procedure Code, the Court considered whether material irregularity in conducting the execution sale had caused substantial injury. Evidence that separate sales of comparable properties produced substantially more than their grouped valuation, together with a finding that separate sales of the properties in question would probably similarly yield a higher price, was sufficient evidence of substantial injury in this case.

predicates.execution_auction_sale_challenge: A party applied to set aside an auction sale held to execute a decree.
predicates.sale_irregularity_found: The court found a material irregularity in the conduct of the sale.
predicates.separate_sale_evidence_supports_higher_p: Evidence from separate sales and the court’s assessment supported that separate lots would probably fetch a higher price than a grouped sale.

issues.definition: When an execution auction sale is challenged, the sale is materially irregular, and evidence supports that separate lots would probably fetch a higher price, substantial injury is found.
